severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum
response.rationale: The parallel origin of both great vessels from the right ventricle is the most specific finding, consistent with a conotruncal anomaly (closest to Tetralogy of Fallot among options), while the VSD is a secondary feature. Tricuspid atresia is contradicted by severe tricuspid regurgitation and right ventricular dilation.

rejected.why: Tricuspid atresia would show absent/atretic tricuspid valve, not severe regurgitation; right ventricle is dilated, not hypoplastic.
VSD is present but is only one component; the parallel great vessel origin is the dominant diagnostic clue.
